headline: The 2 PM HRRR run all but dropped tonight's burst, from 0.27 to 0.02 in in the wettest 3 hours, while ECMWF still holds 0.27 in around 2 to 5 AM; the rating card stays at none, and the bigger story this week remains the king tides on the Bay shore.

summary.text: Down since midday: HRRR's wettest 3 hours fell from 0.27 to 0.02 in, and its 0.24 in peak hour near 2 AM is gone. Consensus slipped from 0.15 to 0.07 in.
Wettest 3 hours: ECMWF 0.27, RRFS 0.15 (older 4 AM run), NBM 0.07, HRRR 0.02 in (GFS copies HRRR). Storm totals 0.02 to 0.37 in. Wide spread; HRRR is now the low outlier.
Rating card consensus 0.07 in: none. A heavier shower could still pond gutters and low spots briefly. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour, far above any model.
Light rain possible from late evening, most likely heaviest 2 to 5 AM Wednesday (ECMWF, RRFS, NBM); HRRR only shows a brief shower near 6:45 to 7 AM. Dry Thanksgiving; light rain possible Sunday.
The 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM runs about 8.5 ft with surge, so drainage is slow until about 3 to 4 AM. Channel low: 0.14 ft at 4 PM, flat all day.
Before dark: clear street drain grates and yard drains. No need to move cars on current guidance. Stay off the Bay shore at the late-morning king tides Wednesday and Thursday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A weakening cold front crosses the Bay Area tonight. NWS San Francisco (short term issued 12:00 PM, unchanged since the last discussion) has the rain band losing energy as it moves south and inland, breaking into scattered showers by the Wednesday commute and ending by afternoon. NWS totals: 0.25 to 0.50 in for San Francisco and the bay shore, 0.5 to 0.75 in on the Peninsula's coastal slopes, under 0.25 in for the South Bay; a 15 percent chance of a few heavier showers or a thunderstorm for coastal areas north of Santa Cruz. The 3:51 PM aviation discussion adds that storm severity has decreased over the last 48 hours and gusty winds with the band are now low confidence. Thanksgiving and Friday dry; light rain likely Sunday, with a stronger trough possible around next Tuesday. The Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines was reissued at 1:42 PM and runs until 4 PM Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
The big change since the 1:20 PM discussion is HRRR. Its 2 PM run removed the 2 AM burst it showed at 11 AM; the only rain left in it for the next 72 hours is 0.02 in near 7 AM Wednesday. That drop alone pulled the consensus down by half. The other models did not get a new look: RRFS is still the 4 AM run, and ECMWF and NBM are essentially unchanged.

Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 4 PM Tuesday onward (72 hours):
• HRRR (2 PM Tue run, out to 10 AM Thu): 0.02 / 0.02 in, a single light shower near 7 AM. Down from 0.27 / 0.32 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Wednesday): a trace near 4:15 AM, then showers 6:15 to 7 AM with the most, 0.031 in, around 6:45 AM.
• RRFS (4 AM Tue run, no newer run yet): 0.15 / 0.15 in, almost all of it (0.12 in) in the hour around 2 AM. Unchanged.
• NBM: 0.07 / 0.11 in, a few hundredths late evening and the rest about 3 to 6 AM. Little changed.
• ECMWF: 0.27 / 0.37 in, still the wettest: about 0.02 in per hour from 11 PM, then 0.09 in per hour around 2 to 5 AM. Unchanged.
• GFS: matches HRRR hour for hour again, so no independent information.

Consensus (HRRR 0.02 × 1.25 = 0.03, RRFS 0.15, NBM 0.07): middle value 0.07 in, down from 0.15 in. The rating card stays at none. I think that is about right this time. HRRR has under-forecast big local bursts here, but even three times its new number is under 0.1 in, and NWS describes a front that is falling apart as it reaches the South Bay. ECMWF's 0.27 in is the realistic worst case: gutters running full for an hour or two, well short of any flooding threshold.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 7 AM Thursday) still runs about 1.1 to 1.4 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City. This evening's -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM runs about -0.2 ft near 7:30 PM, a good window for the channel to drain before any rain.

The 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM Wednesday runs 7.3 ft at midnight, 8.3 ft at 1 AM, a crest near 8.5 ft at 1:30 to 2 AM, 7.7 ft at 3 AM and 6.5 ft at 4 AM. If the ECMWF/RRFS timing verifies, the heaviest rain overlaps the back half of that high, so the channel drains slowly until about 3 to 4 AM. The 3.2 ft low at 6:14 AM runs about 4.3 ft. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM runs about 11.0 ft near noon, after the rain has ended; Thursday's 9.4 ft high is at 12:35 PM.

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge, highs 2.7 ft above normal Wednesday (8.5 ft at 10:49 AM), 2.2 ft Thursday (8.0 ft at 11:38 AM) and 2.0 ft Friday and Saturday, including up to 1.5 to 1.6 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.14 ft at 4 PM, flat between 0.12 and 0.14 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM, still its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry on the street so far. The Caltrain rain gauge still has not reported since 5:13 AM (no rain in the 24 hours to then), so it cannot confirm when rain starts tonight. NWS expects the rain band to reach the airport terminals around 9 PM and become scattered by early morning.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Moderate to high on the amount, low concern for flooding. The models now differ by more than 10× on the wettest 3 hours (HRRR 0.02 in vs ECMWF 0.27 in), but every model is far below the 0.71 in Yellow threshold. The newest data (HRRR 2 PM) is also the driest, and it agrees with NWS's weakening-front story; RRFS is 12 hours old and may come down when a new run arrives. The remaining risk is a single heavier shower that no model places overhead, which would mean brief ponding rather than flooding.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Before dark today: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains; it is cheap insurance for the weekend and next week's possible stronger storm.
• Tonight: no need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac on current guidance. If a downpour does hit overnight, take timestamped photos of the street.
• Stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs and low shoreline roads at the late-morning king tides Wednesday and Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
• Check the next update Wednesday morning.
